before: AutoFit tables scaled authored column widths in proportion to fit their width; older-mode percentage tables with zero cell margins, percent-sign values past their range, text-box tables, and nested tables without a width used the ordinary geometry; mode 15 right-to-left tables mirrored the left-to-right position.
after: AutoFit tables with a preferred width on every column raise columns to their minimums and give way by their spare room; those older-mode tables use the content-aligned reference box with their measured adjustments; mode 15 right-to-left tables move half their mean outer rule toward their visual left.
reason: Only layout geometry changes. Document nodes, text offsets, operations, room formats, and package serialization stay the same.
